kinds.D: doc line to function (control, never pooled with T and C)

rules.T: A test function (in test code, named test*, or marked #[test]) whose name holds, as a run of whole name tokens (split on underscores and capitals), the name of exactly one non-test function of the corpus; a run inside a longer matching run does not count. That function must be defined once in the corpus, called from at most 40 places (a function used everywhere is set-up code in most tests), and called by the test: a call in the call graph (pgr callers), or for a name of two or more tokens a call-shaped mention in the test body. A one-token name must open the test name and be a graph call, because in a sentence-style test name a one-token function name is mostly a coincidence of English words. Query: the remaining words of the test name (test, tests, it, should dropped) plus the test's first doc line when it has one; at least 2 words must be left. Answer: the function.
rules.C: A non-merge commit that changed 1 to 3 source files (extension of the corpus language, outside test paths), all still present at HEAD, in at most 8 changed paths of any kind. Query: the subject with a leading tag, issue numbers and trailing punctuation removed; at least 3 words and at least 3 content words (not a stop word or a generic change verb such as fix, add, update, use, refactor); subjects matching the drop list are dropped first. Answer: any hit in one of those files, a definition or a chunk of the file.
rules.D: Control. Query: a function's own doc line (at least 3 words, unique in the corpus). Answer: that function. Word search should be near perfect here; a low score means the harness is broken.
rules.all: A query never holds the full name of its answer (identifier or whole-token run; for C, the file name, its path or the name of a definition in the answer files). A query that two challenges share with different answers is dropped. An answer is never in an example, doc, docs_src, compat or legacy folder: the engine under test scales most of those paths down on purpose (rank.rs path_penalty) and documentation folders hold build configuration. Hits in test code are skipped before ranking: a path with a test, tests, testing, __tests__, spec or specs folder, a file named test_*, *_test, *_tests, *.test.*, *.spec.*, tests, test or conftest, and Rust code inside a #[cfg(test)] module or marked #[test]. At most 400 challenges per kind and corpus, sampled with a fixed seed. Id is the first 64 bits of a SHA-256 of corpus, kind, query and answer; an odd id is held-out, an even id is tune. Metrics are reported for held-out. Credit for T and D, cover matching (the main numbers): the definition row of the function, a chunk that overlaps the function or the comment lines directly above it, or any hit in the same file whose lines contain the whole function (the class or impl block the engine returns for a method). Exact matching leaves out the containing block. C is file-level in both.

limits: Queries come from developer-written test names and commit subjects, not from questions an agent would ask.
File-level credit for C is lenient: any hit in a changed file counts.
Five corpora in three languages; JavaScript has no named tests (mocha callbacks), so T is empty there and express is judged on C alone.
The hybrid variant was built by people who had seen none of these challenges. Any variant tuned later on the tune half must be judged on the held-out half only.
Pooled rows weight each challenge equally, so the larger corpora count more.
A test-name query and its answer share vocabulary by construction; the numbers compare variants, they are not a forecast of agent behaviour.
Cover matching credits a block that contains the function; a variant that returns coarser blocks gains from it. The exact-matching numbers are kept beside the main ones for that reason.
Answers in example, doc, docs_src, compat and legacy folders are left out because the engine demotes most of them on purpose; a change to that policy is not measured here.
